Workers with Mexico's Social Security Institute are set to march in Nuevo Laredo this afternoon as part of a national day of protest, with the local march scheduled to start at 3:30 p.m. at Plaza Hidalgo — known as Plaza del Reloj — and end at Plaza Esteban Baca Calderón, according to Claro Sports.

The Nuevo Laredo action is one of at least 16 states joining the October 30 mobilization by active and retired IMSS workers, who are pressing for a 10 percent raise applied directly to their base salary, better working conditions, and a reliable supply of medicines and medical supplies, according to the report. Protesters are also calling for the removal of Rafael Olivos Hernández, secretary general of the National Union of Social Security Workers (SNTSS).

The dispute centers on the size and shape of the raise. IMSS Director General Zoé Robledo has proposed an overall 8 percent increase, made up of 4 percent to base salary and 4 percent for housing assistance, according to Claro Sports. The dissident workers argue that split does not meet their demand for the full 10 percent on base pay.

In Mexico City, the national mobilization includes a morning march from IMSS headquarters on Paseo de la Reforma and an afternoon gathering at the National Medical Center Siglo XXI. A national assembly is planned for Saturday, October 31, according to the report.

For Nuevo Laredo residents, the practical takeaway is timing and place: the local march is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. from Plaza Hidalgo to Plaza Esteban Baca Calderón. A related gathering is also planned in Reynosa, on Boulevard Hidalgo, though no time was specified in the report.

Sources:

  • Claro Sports, "Megamarcha IMSS hoy 30 de octubre," October 30, 2026
